terra.problem: Papa describes himself ordering at a drive-through. Things outside his bakery, such as cars, come up as things people do, not things he does.
“Wrong spot” calls the baker’s answer wrong.
The passage does not call this Saul’s first sermon.
The hearers ask whether Saul is the man they know about; the text does not say they knew for certain who he was.
“Nobody in that room” adds a single room and applies the reaction to everyone there. The text says all who heard Saul were astounded.
The text says Saul confounded the Jews in Damascus, not that they had no comeback.
“Stopped them cold” goes beyond the text’s statement that Saul confounded them.
The text does not establish that a cart would have to go through a gate or that none of the disciples crossed the watched gates.
The passage does not say Saul’s reputation reached the disciples before he did.
“Turn that room around” asserts a change in the disciples’ response that the text does not describe.
Saying Barnabas put his own name on the line adds a personal risk the text does not state.
Acts 9:21 reports the hearers asking whether Saul came to take people to the chief priests. The explanation presents their question as an established fact.
This is a plain restatement of the verse without Papa’s distinctive voice.
“That’s some debate” makes light of the attempt to kill Saul by treating it as an extreme debate.
The statement that Antioch is a city in Acts is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The statement that Joppa is a city in Acts is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
